testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is:
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have no more than 3 psi air loss in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: The air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is depressed, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down

questions.explanation: Air brakes take a half-second or more to work after the brake pedal is pushed. This is different from hydraulic brakes in cars, which work instantly.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate that is safe for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have no more than 3 psi air loss in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue if nothing seems wrong

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. You need to maintain braking power while you still have it.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving
Use wheel chocks, but only if you have applied the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is essential if your vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: You should ____ if the low pressure warning signal activates while you are driving.

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates, exit the roadway as soon as you safely can and park your vehicle. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
Shift down instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use engine braking to slow down. Use your brakes only to help the engine braking work.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated in an air brake vehicle, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air brakes could damage the brakes.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does the air compressor governor stop pumping air?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What gets removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil that builds up. If water and oil are left in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The service brake system works when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What does it mean if the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: You can only brake if there is enough air left in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before the air runs out.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later.
You should stay 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if there is enough air left in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. You may have a leak. You can still brake only as long as there is enough air in the tanks.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brakes. These brakes work using compressed air.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning signal turn on?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must activate when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: They let rain water into the air tank.
They remove water and oil from the air tank.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up
Prevent the vehicle from speeding uphill
Prevent the vehicle from speeding downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: The braking mechanisms that stop your vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, make sure brake drums have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before every trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: While driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, hold the brake pedal until your vehicle slows to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.
